title: Why your pupils grow bigger when you see someone you like
hook: Your eyes can betray your true feelings.

narration.text: Your pupils get bigger when you look at something you genuinely like.
This happens automatically, you cannot control it.
It is a sign of physiological arousal.
When aroused, your body activates the sympathetic nervous system.
This system prepares you for action, or for 'fight or flight'.
One side effect is pupil dilation, letting in more light.
So, bigger pupils can signal genuine interest or attraction.
You might notice it when someone is very engaged in a conversation.
Have you ever noticed your own pupils change size?

description: Discover the surprising link between your pupils and what you truly like. It is all part of your body's automatic response system, the sympathetic nervous system, revealing your hidden interests.
topic: Why your pupils get bigger when you see something you like, explaining the link between arousal and autonomic nervous system responses.
